Thanks — quick legal read below. I'm sending a draft redline as an attachment (proposed-redline-msasection6.docx) but key commercial/legal guardrails here:

1) Scope-limited flowdown: we should expressly limit any subcontracting consent to the named subcontractor (LogStream Solutions) and to the narrow parsing scope in the attached SOW. That avoids open-ended delegation.
2) DPA annex: please include an Annex D reference in the MSA amendment that:
   - ties permitted processing activities to the SOW;
   - requires the subcontractor to adhere to the same security controls and breach-notification timelines as Redwood's DPA;
   - prohibits the subcontractor from retaining parsed outputs beyond 30 days unless expressly agreed in writing.
3) Audit and evidence: Redwood will accept SOC2 Type II evidence for the subcontractor plus a signed subprocessor attestation (template attached in the draft). If LogStream's SOC2 scope excludes parsing, we need compensating controls.
4) Staged consent: recommend a staged approval (pilot -> limited production) where initial consent covers only non-sensitive telemetry for up to 30 days; any expansion requires fresh sign-off from Redwood Legal + Security.

Operational asks for CloudSync: please provide the exact DocuSign contact and route (who signs first), and confirm whether the subcontractor will be a party to the DocuSign envelope or will sign separately.

I'll be on PTO 7/30-8/2 but can review an executed DocuSign envelope remotely if needed.

—Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
